title: Sales order entry from email and PDF
problem: Customer service reps re-key purchase orders that arrive as PDF attachments or email text from customers not on EDI.
nativeFirst: Move high-volume customers to EDI or a customer portal first. Automate the long tail that remains.

tasks.name: Extract order header and lines from the customer PO
tasks.note: Every customer sends a different layout, and many orders are email body text. Output creates a draft order, never a posted one.

tasks.name: Map customer item codes and descriptions to your material master
tasks.note: Customer-material info records cover most lines. Fuzzy matching on descriptions handles the rest; confirmed matches feed the info records.

tasks.name: Validate price, availability, and credit before release
tasks.note: Pricing conditions, ATP checks, and credit checks already exist in the ERP. Reuse them on the draft order.

title: Credit hold release
problem: Orders blocked by credit checks wait in a queue while credit analysts review each one, delaying shipment for customers who would have paid.
kpis: Share of holds released without analyst touch
nativeFirst: SAP S/4HANA Credit Management and Oracle credit management support rule-based holds and scoring. Tune those before adding a model.

tasks.name: Apply credit policy (limit, overdue items, blocks)
tasks.note: Credit policy is written down. It stays deterministic.

tasks.name: Score the risk of releasing a held order
tasks.note: Years of release decisions and subsequent payment behavior are in AR history. The score prioritizes and pre-approves low-risk holds; analysts own the rest.

tasks.name: Summarize account context for the credit analyst
tasks.note: Summarizes exposure, payment trend, disputes, and the model's reason codes. It explains; it does not decide.

title: Cash application
problem: Incoming payments arrive with incomplete remittance, and AR staff manually match them to open invoices.
nativeFirst: Check the auto-match rate of your ERP's existing cash application rules and any ML cash-application feature you already license.

tasks.name: Extract remittance details from emails and PDF advices
tasks.note: Remittance advices come in every format. Bank data in them means the model must run under enterprise terms or in-region.

tasks.name: Match payments to open invoices
tasks.note: Invoice numbers, amounts, and customer references carry most of the signal. Partial payments and short-pays need tolerance rules.

tasks.name: Suggest matches for residual unmatched payments
tasks.note: Past manual applications are labels. The model ranks candidate invoice sets for a person to confirm.

title: Collections worklist prioritization
problem: Collectors work accounts by age or size and miss accounts that are about to go late.
nativeFirst: Most collections modules already build worklists by strategy. Replace only the ranking input.

tasks.name: Predict which invoices will be paid late
tasks.note: Payment history per customer is the strongest signal and sits in AR already.

tasks.name: Rank the worklist by expected value at risk
tasks.note: Amount × probability of late payment, sorted. A formula, not a model.

tasks.name: Draft dunning emails tailored to the account
tasks.note: Sending to a customer cannot be undone. The collector reviews and sends.

title: Deduction and dispute resolution
problem: Customers short-pay invoices for pricing, promotions, damages, or shortages. Analysts spend most of their time gathering evidence.
nativeFirst: Standardize reason codes in your dispute management module first; classification accuracy depends on them.

tasks.name: Classify the deduction reason from the customer claim
tasks.note: Historical deductions already carry analyst-assigned reason codes.

tasks.name: Gather evidence (proof of delivery, price agreement, promo terms)
tasks.note: What to look up depends on the reason code and the customer. Read-only access across ERP, TMS, and trade promotion systems.

tasks.name: Decide whether the deduction is valid
tasks.note: Accepting or disputing affects revenue and the customer relationship. The analyst decides from the assembled case file.

title: Supplier delivery risk
problem: Buyers learn about late deliveries when the goods don't arrive, too late to expedite or re-source.
nativeFirst: Confirm supplier confirmations and ASNs are captured consistently; they are the model's best features.

tasks.name: Predict late delivery risk per PO line
tasks.note: PO history with promised vs actual receipt dates is the label. Features: supplier, material, lead time, confirmation status, lane.

tasks.name: Explain the risk drivers to the buyer
tasks.note: Turns the model's reason codes into a sentence. Optional; a well-designed table of reason codes may be enough.

title: Invoice capture and validation
problem: AP keys supplier invoices from PDF and paper, then checks them against vendor master and tax rules.
nativeFirst: Push large suppliers to e-invoicing or a supplier portal. Extraction is for the rest.

tasks.name: Extract header and line fields from supplier invoices
tasks.note: Invoices are a well-served document type. Prebuilt models with confidence scores beat a general LLM on cost at this volume.

tasks.name: Validate against vendor master, PO, and tax rules
tasks.note: Bank detail changes must never be accepted from an invoice. That is a control, not a prediction.

title: Three-way match exception resolution
problem: Invoices that fail PO / goods receipt / invoice matching sit blocked while AP chases buyers and receivers.
nativeFirst: Review tolerance keys in SAP or Oracle match tolerances first. Poorly set tolerances create most exceptions.

tasks.name: Apply price and quantity tolerances
tasks.note: Native ERP functionality. No AI.

tasks.name: Route each exception to the right resolver
tasks.note: Exception type, variance, supplier, and plant predict who resolves it. Past resolutions are the labels.

tasks.name: Summarize the exception and suggested fix
tasks.note: Cuts reading time for the resolver. The suggested fix comes from rules on the variance type, not from the LLM.

title: Spend classification
problem: PO and invoice lines are coded inconsistently, so spend analytics and category strategies run on bad data.
nativeFirst: Enforce category selection on catalog and PO forms for new spend. Classification cleans the backlog and free-text lines.

tasks.name: Classify line descriptions into the category taxonomy
tasks.note: Existing coded lines are the training set. Volume makes per-call LLM cost add up.

tasks.name: Classify new categories that have no labeled examples
tasks.note: An LLM bootstraps labels for new or rare categories; reviewed results retrain the small classifier.

title: Duplicate invoice and payment detection
problem: Duplicate invoices slip through when invoice numbers are keyed differently or submitted through two channels.
nativeFirst: Turn on your ERP's duplicate invoice check and confirm which fields it compares.

tasks.name: Detect exact and near-duplicate invoices before payment
tasks.note: Normalized invoice number, amount, date window, and supplier. Holds the invoice for review; it never cancels one.

tasks.name: Flag unusual invoices and payment patterns
tasks.note: Split invoices, round amounts, new suppliers with high volume. Output is an audit queue.

title: Procurement policy and contract Q&A
problem: Buyers and requesters email procurement to ask which policy applies or what a contract says about terms, rebates, or renewal.
nativeFirst: Get contracts into one repository with metadata. Q&A over scattered files fails on retrieval, not on the model.

tasks.name: Answer questions from policy and contract documents
tasks.note: An LLM is the right tool here. Answers cite the clause, and users see only contracts they are permitted to see.

tasks.name: Extract key terms (payment terms, rebates, expiry, auto-renewal)
tasks.note: Contract language varies too much for templates. Extracted terms populate contract metadata after review.

title: Shipment ETA and delay mitigation
problem: Planners find out about late shipments from customers or carriers, then scramble to re-plan affected orders.
nativeFirst: Get carrier milestone events flowing into the TMS or a visibility platform. Without events, there is nothing to predict from.

tasks.name: Predict ETA and delay risk per shipment
tasks.note: Lane, carrier, milestone timing, and dwell history. Visibility platforms may already provide this; compare before building.

tasks.name: Re-plan affected orders (reallocate stock, expedite, split)
tasks.note: Inventory, customer priority, and expedite cost trade off under capacity limits. The planner approves the plan.

tasks.name: Draft the customer delay notification
tasks.note: Uses the new ETA and the approved plan. Reviewed before sending, or templated if wording must be fixed.

title: Carrier selection and load tendering
problem: Loads are tendered by habit or a static routing guide, missing cheaper or more reliable options.
nativeFirst: Most TMS platforms include an optimizer. Check whether it is configured and used before building one.

tasks.name: Select carrier and mode per load
tasks.note: Rates, capacity commitments, service levels, and allocation targets are constraints. That is a solver problem.

tasks.name: Apply routing guide and contract rules
tasks.note: Hazmat, customer-mandated carriers, and lane restrictions are hard rules applied before and after optimization.

title: Freight invoice audit
problem: Carrier invoices include accessorials and rate errors that go unchecked and get paid.
nativeFirst: Receive EDI 210 invoices where possible; audit is then mostly rules.

tasks.name: Compare billed charges to contracted rates and accessorials
tasks.note: Rate tables and accessorial schedules are explicit. This use case needs little or no AI.

tasks.name: Extract data from non-EDI freight invoices
tasks.note: A known set of carrier layouts. Prebuilt or custom-trained document models.

title: "Where is my order" inquiries
problem: Customer service answers order-status emails and chats by looking up the order, delivery, and shipment in three systems.
nativeFirst: A self-service order-status page removes a large share of these inquiries without any AI.

tasks.name: Look up order, delivery, and shipment status and answer
tasks.note: Read-only tools into ERP and TMS. The customer must be verified before any order data is returned.

tasks.name: Detect complaints and claims that need a person
tasks.note: Damage claims, cancellations, and angry customers route to a person immediately.
